questions.prompt: Explain the difference between NSCache and URLCache in iOS apps. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that URLCache handles raw HTTP network responses across memory and disk according to HTTP headers
Explains that NSCache stores in-memory objects like images and automatically purges items under memory pressure

questions.modelAnswer: URLCache manages HTTP network responses by storing raw data in memory and on disk according to web headers like Cache-Control. In contrast, NSCache is an in-memory key-value collection designed for decoded runtime objects such as images and view models. NSCache automatically purges cached items when the system experiences memory pressure, preventing application crashes.

questions.prompt: Explain what HTTP 304 Not Modified means and how it benefits mobile applications. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that 304 Not Modified tells the client that the cached response is still fresh and has not changed on the server
Explains that it saves mobile network bandwidth and battery by skipping redundant payload downloads

questions.modelAnswer: A 304 Not Modified response tells the client that the requested resource has not changed since the last request. The server sends this status without a response body when validation headers like ETag match. This allows the app to reuse its cached payload, saving cellular bandwidth and battery life.

questions.prompt: Why should developers avoid using a standard Swift Dictionary as an image cache, and what should be used instead? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that standard dictionaries never auto-evict items on memory pressure, leading to out-of-memory app terminations
Explains that NSCache should be used instead because it responds automatically to low memory warnings and provides thread safety

questions.modelAnswer: A standard Swift Dictionary retains all inserted objects indefinitely and does not respond to system memory warnings. In image-heavy apps, this unmanaged memory growth causes the operating system to terminate the application. Developers should use NSCache instead because it automatically purges items under memory pressure and provides thread-safe access.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between URLRequest cache policies useProtocolCachePolicy and returnCacheDataElseLoad. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that useProtocolCachePolicy respects server headers like Cache-Control and validates with the server when expired
Explains that returnCacheDataElseLoad returns cached data regardless of expiration, querying the network only if no cache exists

questions.modelAnswer: The default useProtocolCachePolicy strictly follows HTTP caching rules and server Cache-Control directives, contacting the server when cached data expires. On the other hand, returnCacheDataElseLoad uses existing local cache data regardless of expiration or age. It only initiates a network connection if no cached response exists locally.

questions.prompt: Why is caching decoded bitmap images in memory more efficient during list scrolling than caching raw compressed Data? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that decompressing raw image formats like PNG or JPEG requires heavy CPU processing on each frame
Explains that storing decoded bitmaps in NSCache allows instant GPU rendering without repeated decompression hitches

questions.modelAnswer: Compressed image formats like JPEG or PNG must be decompressed into raw pixel bitmaps before they can be rendered on screen. If only raw Data is cached, the CPU must decompress the image every time a cell scrolls into view, leading to dropped frames. Storing decoded bitmap images in NSCache allows immediate GPU drawing and smooth 60 or 120 FPS scrolling.
